key_insight: Replacing attention-heavy EEG models with causal state-space models enables true real-time, continuous inference over arbitrarily long EEG recordings without sliding-window hacks or quadratic time/space costs.
problem_solved: Addresses the scalability and latency limits of existing EEG deep-learning pipelines that rely on attention and fixed-length windows, which struggle with very long recordings and real-time/streaming requirements.
method: Use causal state-space models (SSMs) as the core temporal backbone to provide linear-time, constant-memory sequence processing instead of quadratic attention.
Design a streaming, sample-by-sample inference pipeline that emits continuous outputs (no sliding windows) with low latency suitable for online EEG.
Optimize training and inference for EEG: causal conditioning, efficient recurrence/unrolled updates, and architecture choices that trade negligible accuracy for large gains in throughput and memory.
impact: Makes long-duration and real-time EEG analysis practical on commodity and edge hardware, lowering compute/memory costs and enabling continuous brain monitoring, BCI, and clinical applications previously limited by attention-based models.
